international.title: JP Morgan boss says he will set ‘example’ in offsetting UK tax hike on banks
international.summary: Jamie Dimon said he would seek to claw back added costs of ‘unfair penalties’ as bank surcharge rises in January Jamie Dimon, the chief executive of JP Morgan, has said he will find ways to offset the chancellor’s tax hike on banks, calling the increase unfair. Speaking at an event in London on Thursday, Dimon said he would seek to claw back the increase and was “setting an example so that [governments] understand the trade-offs of these unfair penalties”.
